cues.en: Now one word about stateful and presentational components.
When we use a store like that, our product and our cart components are still more on the presentational
than on the stateful side because yes, we do use the store there, but we don't really manage the state
inside of the components.
We use the store to manage the state and yes, we use the store in these components.
So they are maybe a bit stateful, but mostly they are still presentational.
Yet if you wanted to, you could of course still follow an even cleaner approach where in the product
component, for example, you simply throw your own custom event or you forward this click.
If it's the only click that can happen here to the products component and in there you interact with
the store.
If that feels better to you, because then the product component is really just about outputting data
and does not interact with the store.
You could do that as well.
But I also see no harm in interacting with the store here.
The key advantage in general of using the store is that we have a central place for managing our data,
which is not inside of a component and which therefore saves us the hassle of passing data around with
props and with custom events.
Not that these techniques would be wrong or bad.
They are great if you need direct component communication and you certainly should not use a store if
you just want to handle a click in the product component in the products component.
So if you have a direct parent child relation, definitely use props and custom events.
But if you have a relation across components that are not directly related like the product and the
cart, then a store is an awesome tool and it's also an awesome tool for general global application
wide state management.
So whenever you have some data that you need in different parts of your application, then a store is
perfect.
